title: Closing a project: five activities and benefits reviews
blurb: Name the five closing a project activities, what each produces, and why post-project benefits reviews are planned by the project but carried out by the business.
question: While closing a project, the project manager reviews the project log and finds a useful lesson about choosing suppliers. Which activity is this, and where is the lesson recorded?

teach.body: Closing a project has five activities. The PM starts with ONE of two preparation activities: prepare planned closure or, if the board has called an early end, prepare premature closure. Then come confirm project acceptance, evaluate the project and request project closure. The PM is responsible for creating the new closure products but may delegate the work.

head: Activity
Key actions
rows: Confirm the project can close; update the project plan with actuals; close the project log; secure and archive project information; prepare closure communications
Record the premature close request; salvage useful work; make products safe; agree what is completed or abandoned
Pass products to the operational and maintenance environment; confirm acceptance
Compare with the baselined PID and approved changes; analyse estimates against actuals; produce the lessons report and end project report
Brief the board on performance; confirm readiness; highlight concessions; recommend recognition

teach.h: End project report vs lessons report

rows.label: Looks at
values: Performance against the PID used to authorize the project
Lessons for this or future projects

rows.label: Includes
values: Product review, benefits review, follow-on actions

rows.label: Made in
values: Evaluate the project, with the PMT

items.label: Benefits management approach kept up to date at boundaries
Benefits realized so far assessed; post-project reviews planned
Board makes sure post-project reviews are covered
The business carries out the benefits reviews

teach.caption: It is not a project activity to carry out post-project benefits reviews, only to plan for them.

teach.h: Practices applied in closing a project

rows.label: Plans: product register checked and closed
Quality: quality register checked and closed
Business case: updated with actual costs and benefits
Organizing: team performance and well-being reviewed

teach.h: Worked scenario: a leisure booking system
teach.body: Ashcombe Leisure Trust's online booking project reaches its planned end. Project manager Ruth Olsen closes the project log and archives the files, then hands the system to the IT service desk and confirms acceptance; senior user Leon Hart checks that post-project benefits reviews are planned. In evaluate the project Ruth compares results with the baselined PID and writes the end project and lessons reports. When requesting closure, she recommends the board thank the supplier's excellent team manager.

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) Post-project benefits reviews are PLANNED in the project and CARRIED OUT by the business after closure. (2) Lessons from the project log go into the lessons report in evaluate the project, not in prepare planned closure. (3) The executive is accountable for evaluating the project; the PM is responsible. (4) Recognition and celebration are recommended in request project closure.

items: Five activities: prepare planned closure OR prepare premature closure, confirm project acceptance, evaluate the project, request project closure.
Products pass to the operational and maintenance environment in confirm project acceptance.
End project report and lessons report come from evaluate the project.
Product and quality registers are checked and closed.
The project plans post-project benefits reviews; the business carries them out.

summary: You can now name the five closing a project activities, place each closing product and RACI role, and explain why benefits reviews are planned by the project but carried out by the business after closure.

A.q: In which closing a project activity is the end project report prepared?
A.why: Evaluate the project reviews performance against the baselined PID and produces the end project report (manual 19.4.4).

whyNot.0: Request project closure briefs the board using the report already prepared.
whyNot.1: Confirm project acceptance hands the products over and confirms acceptance.
whyNot.3: Prepare planned closure confirms the project can close and archives information.

A.q: In which activity are the project's products passed to the operational and maintenance environment?
A.why: In confirm project acceptance the products are passed to the operational and maintenance environment, in one release or in phases (manual 19.4.3).

whyNot.1: Evaluate the project reviews performance and lessons.
whyNot.2: Request project closure asks the board to authorize closure.
whyNot.3: Prepare premature closure salvages work and makes products safe after an early stop.

A.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.
Post-project benefits reviews are [?] by the project but carried out by the business after the project has closed.
A.why: It is not a project activity to undertake post-project benefits reviews, only to plan for them (manual 19.4.3).

whyNot.0: Completing the reviews happens after closure, in the business.
whyNot.1: Benefits are realized in operational use, largely after closure.
whyNot.2: The project does not audit the reviews; it plans them in the benefits management approach.

B.q:
Which two statements about closing a project activities are correct?
1. The project log is closed in confirm project acceptance.
2. Evaluate the project compares performance against the baselined PID.
3. Post-project benefits reviews are carried out in evaluate the project.
4. Project information is secured and archived in prepare planned closure.
B.why: Evaluate the project compares against the baselined PID (2), and prepare planned closure secures and archives project information (4) (manual 19.4.1, 19.4.4).

whyNot.0: Both are false: the log is closed in prepare planned closure, and benefits reviews happen after closure.
whyNot.1: Statement 1 is false: the project log is closed in prepare planned closure.
whyNot.2: Statement 3 is false: post-project benefits reviews are carried out by the business after closure.

B.q: At closure the project manager reviews the project log and identifies a lesson about supplier selection for future projects. Which activity is this?
B.why: In evaluate the project the PM reviews the project log for lessons for future projects and includes them in the lessons report, consulting the PMT (manual 19.4.4).

whyNot.0: Prepare planned closure closes the project log, but identifying lessons is part of evaluate the project.
whyNot.2: Confirm project acceptance is about handover and acceptance.
whyNot.3: Request project closure briefs the board and asks for authorization.

B.q: The project manager wants the board to recognize a supplier's excellent work and recommend the team for future projects. In which activity should this happen?
B.why: In request project closure the PM briefs the board and suggests celebrating success and recognition, for example recommending a high-performing team manager (manual 19.4.5).

whyNot.0: Evaluate the project identifies lessons but does not make the recommendation to the board.
whyNot.1: Confirm project acceptance covers handover of the products.
whyNot.3: Prepare planned closure confirms the project can close and archives information.

C.q: In the evaluate the project activity, which role is accountable, and which is responsible?
C.why: The official RACI for evaluate the project makes the executive accountable and the PM responsible (manual tab 19.2).

whyNot.2: The senior supplier is consulted, not accountable.
whyNot.3: The business layer is not involved in evaluate the project.

C.q: Which practice is applied when the product register is checked and closed, and which when the quality register is checked and closed?
C.why: Checking and closing the product register applies the plans practice; checking and closing the quality register applies the quality practice (manual tab 19.3).

whyNot.2: Neither register belongs to the progress or issues practice.
whyNot.3: The quality register belongs to the quality practice, not progress.

C.q: In confirm project acceptance, who may check that post-project benefits reviews are planned, and who carries out those reviews?
options: The team manager; the project team before closure
Project support; the project manager at closure
The senior supplier; the board in directing a project
The senior user; the business after closure
C.why: The senior user may check that post-project benefits reviews are planned; the reviews themselves are carried out by the business after closure (manual 19.4.3).

whyNot.0: Team managers are not involved, and reviews are not done before closure.
whyNot.1: The PM does not carry out post-project benefits reviews.
whyNot.2: The senior supplier represents suppliers, not benefits, and the board ensures rather than performs the reviews.

reteach.title: Finishing a house build
reteach.question: What does a builder do in the last weeks before handing a new house to its owners?

blocks.h: Tidy up, hand over, review, sign off
blocks.body: The builder files the paperwork and checks nothing is outstanding, hands over the keys and manuals so the owners accept the house, reviews how the job went against the original contract and notes lessons, then asks the client to sign off. Whether the owners end up happier is measured later, by them. That is closing a project: prepare, confirm acceptance, evaluate, request closure, with benefits reviews after.

blocks.text: The builder does not move in to check whether the family is happier a year later. The project plans benefits reviews; the business does them.

explain.body: Confirm the project can close, update the project plan with actuals, close the project log, secure and archive information, and prepare closure communications.

test.q: Which action is part of prepare planned closure?
options: Update the project plan with actuals
Salvage useful work from the project
Brief the board on project performance
test.why: Prepare planned closure includes updating the project plan with actuals, closing the project log and archiving information (manual 19.4.1).

whyNot.1: Salvaging useful work belongs to prepare premature closure.
whyNot.2: The end project report is written in evaluate the project.
whyNot.3: Briefing the board happens in request project closure.

explain.body: The products must pass to the operational and maintenance environment before closure, either in one release or in phases, and acceptance is confirmed.

test.q: What must happen to the products in confirm project acceptance?
options: They are returned to the team managers
They are kept by the project for a year
They pass to the operational environment
They are archived with the project log
test.why: The project's products are passed to an operational and maintenance environment before closure (manual 19.4.3).

whyNot.0: Team managers hand products to the PM during delivery; at closure they go to operations.
whyNot.1: The project ends at closure, so it cannot keep the products.
whyNot.3: Archiving applies to project information, not to the products themselves.

explain.body: The PM reviews the original intent in the baselined PID and approved changes, analyses estimates against actuals to improve future estimating, and produces the lessons and end project reports.

test.q: What does evaluate the project analyse to improve estimating on future projects?
options: The risk appetite against risk tolerance
The benefits against the project mandate
The checkpoint reports against team plans
test.why: Evaluate the project may improve future estimation by analysing estimates and actual progress metrics (manual 19.4.4).

whyNot.0: Risk appetite and tolerance are set by the business and board, not compared here for estimating.
whyNot.2: Benefits are reviewed against the business case, and the mandate is not an estimating baseline.
whyNot.3: Checkpoint reports and team plans are work package level tools used during delivery.

explain.body: The project assesses benefits realized so far and updates the benefits management approach so post-project reviews are planned. The business performs those reviews after closure.

test.q: Which is a project activity in relation to post-project benefits reviews?
test.why: It is a project activity to plan post-project benefits reviews, not to undertake them (manual 19.4.3).

whyNot.0: The business carries out post-project reviews after closure.
whyNot.1: Many benefits are realized after the project closes.
whyNot.3: Business strategy is set by the business layer, outside the project.
